description.narrative: The Project consists of an unsecured senior loan of up to US$25 million equivalent in EUR with a maturity of up to 5 years, including up to 12 months grace period. IFCs own account (O/A) will provide US$10 million, while the remaining US$15 million will be mobilized from other lenders. The financing will be extended to Coris Bank International Senegal with the objective of providing the Bank with stable long-term funding to scale up lending to micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Senegal. At least 25% of the proceeds will be earmarked for women-owned or women-led MSMEs (WSMEs), thereby promoting inclusive access to finance. Subject to further approvals, the Project will be processed under the MSME Finance Platform (the Platform), which is supported by a pooled first-loss guarantee provided by the International Development Association Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA20-PSW BFF), allocated to the SME Envelope under the Platform.

The most significant expected Project-level outcome is the increase in access to finance for MSMEs, including WMSMEs in Senegal. This will help address the large MSME finance gap in Senegal valued at US$1.5 billion, equivalent to over 7% of GDP. Beyond the Project-level outcome, IFC anticipates that the Project, together with other projects with CBI subsidiaries in the region, will promote greater market competitiveness in MSME lending across the financial sector via demonstration and replication effects.
